deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The verso holds two unrelated groups of material. (A) Counting theta characteristics in genus p (Riemann writes p for the genus). (B) A draft letter, in German with a Latin version, proposing the twin-prime problem as a prize question of the Königliche Societät der Wissenschaften zu Göttingen. The previous page is a geodesy report (Baeyer's Gradmessung). The next page is theta/elliptic algebra.

(A) THETA CHARACTERISTICS.
A characteristic is a 2 x p array of bits (a', a''), so there are 2^{2p} theta functions with half-integer characteristic. Parity is e(a) = (-1)^{a'.a''}. 'Anzahl der Classen 2^{2p}-1' is the number of nonzero half-periods w. Each w defines a class pairing a with a+w.

Table on the page:
- alpha_p (odd) = 2^{p-1}(2^p-1).
- beta_p (even) = 2^{p-1}(2^p+1).
- Theta products per class: each class splits the 2^{2p} characteristics into 2^{2p-1} unordered pairs {a, a+w}.
- gamma_p (both odd) = 2^{p-2}(2^{p-1}-1).
- delta_p (one even, one odd) = 2^{2p-2}.
- epsilon_p (both even) = 2^{p-2}(2^{p-1}+1).

Consistency, implicit: 2gamma+delta = alpha, 2epsilon+delta = beta, and gamma+delta+epsilon = 2^{2p-1}.

The two-line expression on the page is the double count of pairs of odd thetas. Each unordered pair of odd characteristics {a,b} determines exactly one class w = a+b. Hence binom(alpha_p,2) = gamma_p (2^{2p}-1).
- With alpha_p = 2^{p-1}(2^p-1), binom(alpha_p,2) = 2^{p-2}(2^p-1)(2^{2p-1}-2^{p-1}-1).
- The factor 2^{2p-1}-2^{p-1}-1 = (2^{p-1}-1)(2^p+1).
- So binom(alpha_p,2) = 2^{p-2}(2^{p-1}-1)(2^p+1)(2^p-1) = gamma_p(2^{2p}-1). This is my reading of the two lines.

'Beweis' (induction p -> p+1). Write a characteristic of genus p+1 as (a, c), with a of genus p and c of genus 1. Parity multiplies. Of the four genus-1 characteristics, three are even and one (11) is odd.
- Hence alpha_{p+1} = 3alpha_p + beta_p and beta_{p+1} = 3beta_p + alpha_p.

For a class W = (w, w1) there are three cases.

Case 0) w != 0, w1 = 0. Pairs {(a,c),(a+w,c)}. An even c (3 choices) keeps both parities; the odd c flips both.
- delta_{p+1} = 4delta_p.
- gamma_{p+1} = 3gamma_p + epsilon_p.
- epsilon_{p+1} = 3epsilon_p + gamma_p.

Case 1) w = 0, w1 != 0 (label '0,0,1'). In genus 1 a nonzero w1 gives one even-even pair and one even-odd pair. The correct result is:
- gamma_{p+1} = alpha_p.
- epsilon_{p+1} = beta_p.
- delta_{p+1} = alpha_p + beta_p = 2^{2p}.
The handwriting in this line is unclear.

Case 2) w != 0, w1 != 0. For each genus-p pair there are 4 choices of c: two with (c, c+w1) even-even, and two mixed (c odd, or c+w1 odd).
- An odd-odd pair gives 2 gamma and 2 delta.
- An even-even pair gives 2 epsilon and 2 delta.
- A mixed pair gives 2 delta, 1 epsilon and 1 gamma.
- So delta_{p+1} = 2delta_p + 2gamma_p + 2epsilon_p, gamma_{p+1} = delta_p + 2gamma_p, and epsilon_{p+1} = delta_p + 2epsilon_p, exactly as on the page.

The closed forms satisfy all three case-recursions. Together with the genus-1 start (gamma_1=0, delta_1=1, epsilon_1=1), this proves by induction that the counts are the same for every one of the 2^{2p}-1 classes. That is the point of the computation.

Other fragments in group A:
- The 0/1 blocks at the top are lists of characteristics (bit arrays), presumably a sample system.
- 'Künftig(?) die Anordnung zu entnehmen aus den syzygetischen' plans to take the ordering from syzygetic systems.
- (p-1)(p-3)/4 is an isolated, unexplained count.
- The index triples 135,136,145,146 / 235,... / 735,... over symbols 1..9,X look like hyperelliptic-style labels of characteristics by branch-point indices. Ten points would mean p=4.

(B) PRIZE QUESTION.
This is a draft letter to 'Hochgeehrter Herr Ober-Medicinalrath'. That is almost certainly Friedrich Wöhler, secretary of the Göttingen Society. Riemann proposes as the next public prize question whether there are infinitely many prime pairs differing by 2.
- Latin: 'In tabulis numerorum primorum quousque pergitur, semper numeri primi inveniuntur, quorum differentia = 2, unde valde verisimile est seriem horum numerorum nunquam abrumpi. Jam postulat Soc. R. literarum, ut argumentis firmis dijudicetur, utrum multitudo binorum numerorum primorum duabus tantum unitatibus differentium infinita crescat nec ne.' An earlier fragment reads '... demonstratione vigorosa muniatur, aut'.
- German: 'In den Primzahltafeln findet man, wie weit man auch fortgehen möge, immer noch Primzahlen, deren Differenz = 2 ist ... Die K. S. d. Wissenschaften verlangt nun, daß durch strenge Beweise entschieden werde, ob die Anzahl Primzahlen, die um zwei Einheiten verschieden sind, unendlich ist oder nicht.' It is signed B. Riemann.
- No mathematics is attempted; it is a problem statement only.
errors: No genuine mathematical errors found; all closed forms and all case recursions check out.

The case-1 line (w=0, w1!=0) is hard to read. The correct relations are gamma_{p+1}=alpha_p, epsilon_{p+1}=beta_p, delta_{p+1}=alpha_p+beta_p=2^{2p}. If the page really reads delta_{p+1}=delta_p, gamma_{p+1}=gamma_p, epsilon_{p+1}=epsilon_p (as the machine transcription has it), that would be wrong; it is more likely a misreading.
The binomial identity relies on each pair of odd characteristics lying in exactly one class (w = a+b). This is true but is left implicit.

The fact that exactly half the pairs in a class are mixed (delta_p = 2^{2p-2}) follows from the bilinear term <a,w> being a nonconstant linear form for w != 0. It is not stated on the page but is proved by the recursion.

results.what: Number of odd/even theta characteristics in genus p: 2^{p-1}(2^p-1) and 2^{p-1}(2^p+1), with recursion alpha_{p+1}=3alpha_p+beta_p
results.modern_name: Counting odd/even theta characteristics (Arf invariant / quadratic forms over F_2)

results.what: For each nonzero half-period, distribution of the 2^{2p-1} theta pairs into odd-odd, mixed and even-even, with counts 2^{p-2}(2^{p-1}-1), 2^{2p-2}, 2^{p-2}(2^{p-1}+1), proved independent of the class by a three-case induction
results.modern_name: Orbit/coset counts of quadratic forms under translation by 2-torsion; theta-pair (Göpel/Rosenhain-type) combinatorics
results.usually_credited_to: Frobenius (1880, 'Über das Additionstheorem der Thetafunctionen...'), Weber (genus 3, 1876)

results.modern_name: Double counting of pairs of odd characteristics

results.what: Proposal of the twin-prime problem (infinitude of primes differing by 2) as a Göttingen Royal Society prize question, letter to the Secretary (Wöhler)

deep.surprise_reason: The theta-characteristic counts are routine and in Riemann's own circle of ideas. A small point of interest is the careful inductive proof that the pair counts are independent of the class. The draft proposing the twin-prime problem as an official Göttingen prize question, with an explicit request for a rigorous proof, is a notable historical detail. It shows Riemann regarded twin primes as a serious open problem and tried to institutionalize it. It is not a mathematical priority claim, since de Polignac stated the conjecture in 1849. I am unsure how widely this draft is known in the literature.
